title: Worker seriously hurt
shows: A serious injury on the list sets the 3-hour clock (INC-a, T3-INJURY).
report: Got a call from Mike on the night crew around 4:30 pm. Said Joe slipped off the valve platform while doing maintenance. Landed hard, couldn’t stand. Called ambulance—took him to Bluewater Health in Sarnia. Leg’s broken, femur. Line stayed shut, no product went anywhere. Mike re-checked the valve—still secure, no leak. Joe was solo on the platform, no one saw him fall. That’s all we got right now.
rationale: All deciding facts stated.

title: Dead fish in a wetland
shows: Visible harm to a wetland is a significant effect: reportable, 24 hours.
report:
Subject: Possible ground movement near creek – Fort St Johns

Hey compliance,

Just spotted some kind of ground shift near the creek crossing west of our ROW outside Fort St Johns. Got a call from a crew at 15:00 today, went out and saw dead fish and vegetation down in the wetland. No product on the ground or in the water, valves all holding. Looks like something undermined the bank—maybe construction gear from that road job we heard about—but haven’t confirmed.

Will keep an eye on it. Let me know if you need anything else.

Tom
Field Operator, Okanagan Crossing Pipelines Ltd.
rationale: All deciding facts stated.

title: Fire, people sheltering
shows: A fire at the facility with people sheltering from smoke: 3 hours.
report:
Got a call from Jim at the Bindloss site. Around 0957 this morning, maintenance crew hit a fire. Working on a pipeline fitting—think it was an elbow, welded. Smoke/fumes got bad enough people had to evacuate or shelter in place. No product leaked from the line, fire was just on our equipment or work area. That’s all I’ve got for now. Will follow up if more comes in.

—Lisa, Control Room Op
rationale: All deciding facts stated.

title: Run outside design limits
shows: Operating outside design limits is reportable on its own (INC-f), 24 h.
report:
Hey, got a call from Shane in the field. SCADA flagged something at Saint Lazare around 17:30 today. No leak, nothing released, but looks like the line was running outside design limits. He’s not sure how long it was like that—just caught it on the screen. Pressure was spiking above the max rating, but no alarms went off until SCADA kicked in. Local tech checked the site, said everything’s holding but the numbers don’t lie. Sent him to pull the chart to see how far over it went. Not sure yet if it’s a sensor issue or actual flow, but either way, it’s off-spec. Will update when we know more.

— Jamie, Control Room Op
rationale: All deciding facts stated.

title: Spill, volume unknown
shows: A missing volume can't be assumed small: precautionary, and the follow-up asks.
report:
Got a call this am from the Williamstown station. Relief valve on line 2A let go around 0845. Gasoline sprayed past the valve stack, hit the RoW gravel and ran downslope into the neighbour's corn. I walked the line by 0915—see the pool on the east edge of the RoW, about 10 m into the crop.

Station crew already had the block valve shut. Relief still lifting, threads on the dummy cap look stripped. Not sure if the diaphragm failed or if someone bumped the set point. Will get the valve tech out this pm.
rationale: Deciding fact missing: PREC gives a precautionary notice and asks the field.

title: Leak, product not named
shows: Without the product, the worst plausible case sets the deadline.
report:
Just got to site near Chetwynd. Leak on branch connection at meter set. Noticed at 3:30 pm today. Threaded fitting blew—gasket shredded. Product sprayed onto ROW, didn’t go past fence. Meter log shows 114 m³ released. Shut downstream valve, called in crew. Still securing area. Will dig up fitting in morning.

— Jake, Area Supervisor
rationale: Deciding fact missing: PREC gives a precautionary notice and asks the field.

title: Spill, location unknown
shows: Where the product went decides 3 h vs 24 h; missing, so 3 h and a question.
report:
Hey Compliance,

Routine walkover on Line 4 near Edmonton this morning. Found oil sheen in low spot around the 12 o’clock position of a girth weld on the 24" mainline. Called in, crew isolated section by 09:30. Meter at block valve shows 8.0 m³ of synthetic crude out.

Shut-down held, vacuum trucks on site by 11:00. Cut-out shows pitting and cracking inside the elbow upstream of the weld—looks like internal corrosion. Sent photos to Engineering. Replacement spool already fabricated, should be in the ground by tomorrow.

Let me know if you need any more details.

Jared
Area Supervisor, Aspen Ridge Pipelines Inc.
rationale: Deciding fact missing: PREC gives a precautionary notice and asks the field.

title: Planned venting
shows: Venting through a working relief valve during maintenance is excluded.
report:
Got a call from the on-call. They told me about an event at our compression station near Moyie, BC. On Aug 13 at 03:00, they did some planned maintenance and a relief valve worked as designed, venting sweet natural gas. The metered volume released was 850 m³ and the release rate was 2 kg/s. They said it was all done on purpose as part of the maintenance. The gas stayed inside the station fence. That's all I got. 
- J. Smith, CRO
rationale: Below the line: planned-venting.

title: Broken finger
shows: A finger fracture alone is not a serious injury (operator policy P3).
report:
Subject: pipe bend issue near Fort McMurray

Compliance,

Walking the right-of-way east of pump station 7 this afternoon—checked the 16-inch main around 14:30. Saw a 45° bend (tag B-12) sitting about 60 cm higher than spec, soil washed out underneath. Pipe isn’t leaking, pressures look normal.

While taking photos, Dave slipped on ice and jammed his left ring finger pretty bad—sent him to the Fort McMurray clinic.

Need someone to look at the bend support and ditch stability.

Jesse
Field Op, Okanagan Crossing Pipelines Ltd.
rationale: P3: a finger or toe fracture alone is not a serious injury.

shows: About 0.1 m³ of lube oil with no harm to water or wildlife: not reportable.
report: "found lube oil release at Hardisty pump station at 02:55. SCADA alerted us. est vol is about 0.1 m³. all inside station fence. small sheen on gravel inside fence, cleaned up same shift. no impact to water or wildlife. that's all for now. - J. Smith, Pipeline Patrol" "update: still checking what happened, but looks like it was contained. will keep you posted if we find more info. - J. Smith, Pipeline Patrol"
rationale: Below the line: minor-env.

title: Mud at a wetland's edge
shows: Nobody has confirmed any got in: precautionary, judgment (policy P1).
variant: U1 mud not confirmed in water
report:
Subject: drilling fluid release near Hope BC

Hey compliance,

Patrol flight spotted drilling rig just east of Hope at 13:51 on Sept 3. Rig pad right beside Prairie Midstream ROW. Meter showed 2.0 m³ drilling mud escaped. Mud ran down slope, crossed the ROW, and pooled at wetland/creek edge. Ground crew threw up silt fence before I left, but nobody’s checked if any made it into the water yet.

Looks like contractor didn’t adjust for the heat—ground’s dry and cracking. No signs they called it in themselves.

Let me know if you need photos or follow-up.

Jake
Pipeline Patrol Contractor
rationale: P1: mud seen in water or a wetland is significant; here nobody has confirmed any got in.

title: Broken collarbone
shows: A fracture not on the CER's list: precautionary 3 h until a filer advises (P3).
report:
"just got to kp 234 near Boyle, AB - found a worker on the ground, collarbone broken, 12:40 today. they were taken to hospital. no release or leak from pipeline. was part of scheduled patrol for Okanagan Crossing Pipelines Ltd. operation was ongoing. will send more info when i get it. - J. Smith, Patrol Contractor" 
"update: confirmed no product was released, still investigating what happened to the worker, 12:40 is confirmed time of finding the worker" - J. Smith, Patrol Contractor
rationale: P3: a collarbone isn't on the major-bone list, and isn't a finger or toe; open until a CER filer advises (Q-7).

title: Estimate near 1.5 m³
shows: An estimated 1.6 m³ can fall either side of the line: judgment (P6).
report:
hey, just got word from the field near Taylor, BC. we had a release of lube oil on the 14th at 23:30. still trying to get all the details. from what i know, it was approx. 1.6 m³. it all stayed inside the station fence. not sure what caused it, was doing some maintenance and there was a lot of lightning in the area. will send more info as i get it. 
- J. Smith, CRO
rationale: An estimate of 1.6 m³ can fall either side of 1.5 m³.

shows: Reportable either way; only 3 h vs 24 h is open, so not precautionary (X1).

Dave
Area Supervisor, Aspen Ridge

title: Inside the fence or in the ditch?
shows: Two accounts disagree on location: reportable, the stricter 3 h (G7).
report: Found crude oil spill at Gretna station 09:50 this AM. Meter shows 2.5 m³ sweet crude. Op says it’s all inside fence. Landowner says oil in road ditch outside fence too—haven’t checked which is right yet. Heavy rain all night, ground’s soft. Tank looked like it was overfilled—no one was watching levels. Will send pics once signal’s back.
rationale: The report places the spill inside the fence and in the road ditch.

title: Two volume estimates
shows: One says under 1.5 m³, one over: whether it's reportable is open (G8).
report:
Subject: crude oil release at Fort McMurray station

We had a crude oil release at our Fort McMurray station last night, discovered at 20:45 on Jan 20. One of our crew members was on site and saw it. The release was contained within the station fence. We're still assessing the volume - one crew member estimates around 0.5 m³, another says about 4 m³. We haven't gotten a meter reading yet to confirm. The product released is sweet crude oil. I'm on site now and will update as soon as I have more info.

The crew is still investigating. I'll send an update as soon as we have a confirmed volume.

S. Jenkins, Area Supervisor
rationale: Two volumes are given (0.5 and 4.0 m³) on either side of 1.5 m³.

title: Sweet gas, but an H2S alarm
shows: An alarm on a sweet line: reportable, 3 h until H2S is ruled out (G9).
report:
Got a leak at Sherwood Park station. Found it 08:49 this morning. Meter says 300 m³ out. Looks like it's through the pipe body or a weld—don't know which yet. Whole thing stayed inside the fence.

Carrying sweet gas, but the H2S monitor on my belt went off at the leak. Still not fixed yet. Crew's on it but no resolution. Just wanted to get this out quick.
rationale: One message says sweet gas, a later one says the H2S monitor went off.
